strongest_angle: Recent studies from Beijing Jiaotong University and Network Rail reveal how human-machine interaction models shift metro drivers from tense operation to severe boredom and vigilance loss.

key_facts.fact: Yiting Wang and researchers at Beijing Jiaotong University published a study in Human Performance titled Not so Tense, but Becoming Boring! A Study on Human-Machine Interaction and Metro Drivers’ Safety Performance.
Aleksandrs Rjabovs from Network Rail and Roberto Palacín from Newcastle University published an eye-tracking study on metro drivers in Urban Rail Transit.

Peter Spring, Andrew McIntosh, Carlo Caponecchia, and Melissa T. Baysari at Macquarie University investigated the impact of train automation levels on driver vigilance using forty student participants.

numbers.label: Student participants in Macquarie University vigilance study
